# Image thumbnails

## What it's for

A gallery, a product list or a profile page shows many images small. Sending each one full size is slow on a phone.
PocketBase can make thumbnails of a file field on request (`?thumb=100x100`); a module lets you make your own when the
file is uploaded: a fixed size, a PNG whatever came in, kept in its own field you can query and send anywhere. The
module uses the [image](https://crates.io/crates/image) crate, built with PNG and JPEG only.

## The route

A `photos` collection with two file fields, `image` (what the user uploads) and `thumb`. An API route takes the
upload (a multipart form with an `image` field) and saves the photo with its thumbnail:

```ts
// pb_pages/photos.ts: an uploaded photo is saved with a 256 px PNG thumbnail in its thumb field
export async function post(ctx: any) {
  if (!ctx.auth) throw ctx.httpError(401, "Sign in to upload")
  const [file] = ctx.req.files("image")
  if (!file) throw ctx.httpError(400, "No image")
  const reader = file.reader.open()
  let bytes: Uint8Array
  try {
    bytes = new Uint8Array(toBytes(reader))
  } finally {
    reader.close()
  }
  const thumb = await $wasm.run.async<{ width: number; height: number; png: string }>("thumbnail", bytes)
  const photo = new Record(ctx.app.findCollectionByNameOrId("photos"))
  photo.set("image", file)
  photo.set("thumb", $filesystem.fileFromBytes(Array.from(Buffer.from(thumb.png, "base64")), "thumb.png"))
  ctx.app.save(photo)
  return ctx.res.json(201, { id: photo.id })
}
```

`ctx.req.files` gives the files uploaded with this request, ready for a record field. A `Uint8Array` goes to the module
as raw bytes. The module answers with JSON, `{width, height, png}`, the PNG as base64; `$filesystem.fileFromBytes`
takes the bytes as a plain array, hence `Array.from`.

## The module

[`src/main.rs`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/wasm/example/thumbnail/src/main.rs) reads the image, scales it to fit, and writes a PNG:

```rust
let size = match std::env::args().nth(1).as_deref() {
    Some("run") => 256,
    Some("small") => 64,
    // ...
};
let img = image::load_from_memory(&input)
    .unwrap_or_else(|e| fail("bad_image", &format!("not a PNG or JPEG image: {e}")));
let thumb = if img.width() > size || img.height() > size { img.thumbnail(size, size) } else { img };
```

`run` fits the image in 256×256 and `small` in 64×64, kept in proportion (`$wasm.call.async("thumbnail", "small",
bytes)` for the small one). It also takes the image as base64 text, which is how its manifest's examples pass one.

## Build

```sh
cd ext/wasm/example/thumbnail
cargo build --release --target wasm32-wasip1   # rustup target add wasm32-wasip1 first
cp target/wasm32-wasip1/release/thumbnail.wasm pb_hooks/thumbnail.pb.wasm
```

## Cost

448 KB. The first call compiles it (about 110 ms); later calls load it from the cache in about 4.5 ms. Decoding is most of the run: a 1280×853 JPEG takes about 230 ms, a
1920×1280 one about 460 ms, a 2560×1706 one about 780 ms (2026-11-18, a laptop).

## Limits

- The decoded image has to fit in the call's memory, 32 MB by default (`MaxCallMemoryMB`): 3 bytes a pixel, so up to
  about 2560×1706 with the defaults. A 4000×2666 photo fails with `crashed` and a message naming the limit; raise
  `MaxCallMemoryMB` (and the timeout) for big camera photos.
- The upload is at most 4 MB (`MaxPayload`).
- PNG and JPEG only. WebP, GIF and others are one Cargo feature each on the `image` crate, and make the module bigger.
